observable_outcome: internal/scheduler decides over multiple Runners and multiple Repositories from a multi-factor domain.PriorityAssessment instead of a bare scalar, records one auditable Decision per candidate with exactly one closed-set reason when it is not assigned, holds an asserted starvation bound under a single Repository's failure-and-retry flood, converges after a cross-repository rollback, detects installation-wide resource conflicts, and completes a 100-candidate tick inside the 30 second reconcile budget -- all in the local closure, with the M7 gate explicitly left to V2-031.
acceptance_criteria: A1. Scope boundary, stated before any code is written. This task proves the local closure only: one process, one test binary, injected clocks, no second OS process, no container, no namespace, no real Provider CLI, no external repository write. The evidence must contain a table with one row per M7 completion condition (two-or-more independent Runner execution entities across two-or-more Repositories; no duplicate owner for the same Increment; no starvation of other important Requirements under one Repository's failure storm; cross-repository rollback converges) stating for each what V2-030 proves in the local closure and what remains unproven and owned by V2-031. The evidence must state in plain words that V2-030 does not pass the M7 gate.

A2. Baseline. Record, before changing anything, that internal/scheduler contains exactly these five top-level tests and that all five pass: TestDecideCrossRepositoryUsesOneRunnerAndApplyIsAtomic, TestDecidePreventsDoubleOwnerAndIsolatesFailureStorm, TestDecideReadSharingWriteExclusionAndProviderCapacity, TestDecideDependencyDAGAndAging, TestDecideBoundsCandidateInput. All five must still pass under exactly these names at the end, with their existing assertions unchanged. Report the before and after top-level test counts.

A3. PriorityAssessment connection. internal/scheduler imports internal/domain (read-only; no other new import) and Requirement carries an optional domain.PriorityAssessment. The score becomes a documented function of ValueScore, UrgencyScore, RiskScore, DependencyScore, LearningScore, ResourceCost and StarvationRisk plus age, with the weighting written down in the source as a comment that says why each factor has the sign and weight it has. domain.PriorityAssessment.Executable == false must exclude the candidate from assignment. Assessment.Version, Reason and ReevaluateWhen must be carried through into the candidate's Decision record. Prove that when no assessment is supplied the resulting order is identical to the current scalar path: assert it directly on a fixture of at least eight candidates with mixed Priority and CreatedAt, comparing the ordered requirement id sequence produced with and without the multi-factor branch.

A4. Decisions. Plan gains a Decisions field carrying one record per candidate considered, with the requirement id, the factor inputs actually used, the computed score, the rank, whether it was assigned, and -- when it was not -- exactly one reason value. The reason values are declared as a closed set of exported constants covering every rejection path Decide has: not-ready, unmet-dependency, repository-unavailable, already-owned, resource-conflict, no-runner-capacity, not-executable. Assert (a) every considered candidate has a decision record, (b) every unassigned candidate has exactly one non-empty reason, (c) every assigned candidate has none, and (d) the reason set is exhaustively enumerated by a table test that fails if a constant is added without a scenario or a scenario without a constant. Existing tests must not be rewritten to compare whole Plan values.

A5. Starvation bound. This is the M7 condition that is currently unproven; TestDecidePreventsDoubleOwnerAndIsolatesFailureStorm proves failure-storm isolation, which is a different property. Build a scenario where one Repository floods the candidate set with a stream of requirements and retries while a high-value requirement bound to a second Repository waits, with runner and provider capacity too small to serve everyone in one tick. Drive a bounded loop of Decide/Apply ticks with an injected clock (no sleep, no timer, no goroutine) and assert the waiting requirement is assigned within a named exported-or-documented constant maximum number of ticks. Write down why that number is the bound before tuning the aging term. Add the negative control: with the aging/StarvationRisk term neutralised, the same scenario must provably fail to converge inside the same bound. Record both directions and the measured tick counts.

A6. Cross-repository rollback convergence. Keep the existing partial-plan assertion. Add: (a) a plan whose claim on the second Repository conflicts leaves zero new claims and zero requirement status changes, with the returned snapshot comparing equal to the pre-Apply snapshot; (b) the immediately following Decide/Apply cycle over that same snapshot reaches a complete assignment for the cross-repository requirement, with no duplicated claim and no duplicated assignment; (c) a third cycle is a no-op, proving convergence rather than oscillation. Assert the claim multiset, not just its length.

A7. Installation-wide resource scope. ResourceRequest.Global has no test today. Add one: a global write claim excludes a same-named resource request raised from a different Repository, a global read shares with a global read, and a repository-scoped claim on the same resource name does not exclude a request in another Repository. Assert the repository id actually recorded on each planned Claim (empty for global, the repository id otherwise).

A8. Reconcile budget. With 100 candidates spread over at least two Repositories and at least two Runner records, Decide plus Apply completes inside a context.WithTimeout of 30 seconds (validation.md section 5: one reconcile tick is at most 100 items within 30 seconds). The deadline is the assertion; the measured duration is logged as an observation and must not be asserted as a threshold. Also record the measured duration at 10, 50 and 100 candidates as observations, and assert the candidate bound still fails closed with ErrCandidateLimit at 101 candidates and at CandidateLimit+1.

A9. Purity, proven mechanically. Add an import scan over internal/scheduler's own *.go files using go/parser, modelled on internal/domain/source_guard_test.go: the allowed import set is the standard library plus internal/domain only, and the scan fails outright if it reads zero files so a broken glob cannot pass vacuously. This is what makes docs/operations/scheduler-local.md's 'no Firestore, network, process or provider operation' claim and validation.md section 5's growth-rate items mechanically true rather than reviewed.

A10. Determinism. No fixed sleep, no timer, no goroutine anywhere in the new tests; every wait is a bounded deadline poll over an injected clock. Run devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 ./internal/scheduler three times in sequence and record that the verdict line and the output are identical each time, and run it once with -race.

A11. Documentation. Update docs/operations/scheduler-local.md to describe: the multi-factor priority and which domain.PriorityAssessment fields feed it, the fallback that keeps the scalar order identical when no assessment is supplied, the Decision record and its closed reason set, the starvation bound constant and what it means, the installation-wide Global scope, the 100-item/30-second budget, and one explicit sentence saying this package is the local closure and that the M7 gate needs V2-031's independent Runner execution entities. Do not edit any other document.

A12. Measured note for V2-045. Record in the evidence that internal/scheduler now imports internal/domain while ci/components.json declares the scheduler component with no dependencies, so the scheduler evidence key does not cover domain's public contracts. Do not edit ci/components.json; name V2-045 as the owner. Record likewise that editing docs/operations/scheduler-local.md moves the docs component key, that only the scheduler record is issued here, and that the docs key movement is resolved by V2-045's component re-issue under gate rule G6.

A13. Evidence. Create .agents/v2/evidence/V2-030-scheduler.json (id ev-v2-030-scheduler, task_id V2-030, component scheduler, correlation_id v2-030-multi-scheduling) recording for every check the argv actually executed, the working directory, the timeout, and a summary that states the measured result. Every acceptance item above must be traceable to a named check. A skipped test is recorded with status skipped and is never counted as a pass (gate rule G7). Record the execution environment identifier (uname -srm, go version, devbox environment). Register it with exactly one appended entry in .agents/v2/evidence/index.json whose evidence_hash is the sha256 of the artifact's final committed bytes; touch no other task's entry. devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 ./internal/contracts must be green with the record in place (TestTaskPacketsValidate and TestActiveEvidenceIndex).

A14. The evidence_key recorded in the artifact is the scheduler component key read with devbox run --pure -- make evidence-keys on the final tree where make check is green, with every touched file already git-added -- a new file that has not been added to the index is invisible to that key.
A15. devbox run --pure -- make check is green, and it is re-run after the evidence commit so the secret scan reads committed history rather than an uncommitted tree. Record both runs.
A16. No file outside allowed_paths changes. ci/components.json, Makefile, go.mod, go.sum and devbox.* are untouched.
constraints: Work only inside the assigned isolated task worktree; never push.
Never use git reset, git checkout --, git stash or git commit --amend.
